cities.d: the "Daughter of the Baltic", Finland's capital and largest city by far

x.around: All public transport within the Capital Region is coordinated by HSL. This means that all public transport, such as trains, trams, buses, ferries and the metro all use the same ticketing scheme. You only need to know which zones you will travel through (see below).

hidden.d: A museum about money and banking, as the name reveals.
The sometimes unusual collections mostly include works by contemporary Finnish artists and artists from nearby countries. There are also periodical exhibitions. The building is a work of art.
Located between the market square (Kauppatori) and the two Esplanadi boulevards, this small but stately park has a commanding position at the heart of the city.

A classic statue designed by the Finnish sculptor Felix Nylund, depicting three nude men hammering down on an anvil (except a study revealed that if the smiths were to actually hammer, they would hit each other on the head).
The beautiful National Library has books all the way from the early 19th century accessible for everyone (and books older than this are kept away from the public).

A beautiful park by the sea in the southernmost part of the city. In summer you might want to sit down for a cup of coffee in one of the seaside cafes and enjoy the view of sailboats and the people on the promenade.
Also known as Kolmikulma (the triangle), this pocket sized park is a nice place to take break from your sightseeing in the summer and just sit down on a park bench and have an ice-cream.
The station building, clad in granite, was designed by Eliel Saarinen (the father of Eero Saarinen) and inaugurated in 1919.

x.intro: Helsinki (Swedish: Helsingfors) is Finland's capital and largest city. Helsinki combines modern and historic architectural styles with beautiful open spaces. The city is surrounded by hundreds of tiny islands, and is a cultural bridge between the East and West. The "Pearl of the Baltic Sea" is easy to explore on foot or on bike, and it has a laid-back vibe.

must.d: The unofficial symbol of the city, this striking white cathedral dominates the central Senate Square. Based on designs by Carl Ludvig Engel and completed in 1852, the cathedral has been refurbished, and the 12 Apostles are on the…
It was built for the Olympics and renovated for the 2005 World Athletic Championships. In the stadium building you can visit the Sports Museum with medals and other paraphernalia related to sport.
A beautiful classical building houses this old museum, which has been renovated. The exhibit includes displays of artefacts and items relating to Finland's history. Closed until spring 2027.
Designed by Finland's best known architect Alvar Aalto. It is across the street from the National Museum. The marble Finlandia Hall is a popular congress and concert venue in Helsinki.
An atmospheric of minimalistic church, this church was literally dug out of solid rock. From above, it resembles a crashed UFO. The roof is made of 22 km of copper strips.
A classical and prominent onion-domed Russian church, the largest Orthodox church in Western Europe, Uspenski Cathedral serves Finland's small Orthodox minority.

The world-famous composer Jean Sibelius' monument was designed by sculptress Eila Hiltunen and unveiled in 1967. It is one of the most well-known tourist attractions in Helsinki as nearly every guided tourist tour is brought to…

Helsinki's equivalent to Arlington in Washington D.C., Hietaniemi is the final resting place for many Finns of importance during the last 200 years: politicians including almost all heads of state, artists and other cultural…

next.d: in Espoo, a piece of untamed wilderness ca 25 km from Helsinki city centre. Accessible by bus from the city.
the second oldest town in Finland is just 60 km away. It has a charming old town of wooden houses. Much more lively in the summer.
the second largest city region in Finland, and the birthplace of Finnish industry, boasting one of the last Lenin museums left in the world as well as a spy museum.
100 km north is famous for the Häme castle, a large medieval castle, and the beautiful park area Aulanko. One hour by train.
the oldest town in Finland, the main one into the 19th century, now third largest city region. The cathedral and the medieval castle are well worth visiting. Two hours by train.
the southernmost spot in Finland, 140 km west of Helsinki. This town of less than 10,000 people is famous for its summer activities, including sandy beaches, sailing, tennis, art, theatre, etc.
the biggest city in Northern Finland (as well as the whole Northern part of the Nordics). Known as the biking and IT capital of Finland and easily accessible from Helsinki, only an hour's flight…
Saint Petersburg, "the Venice of the North", is one of the most beautiful cities in the world. Accessible by St.

x.safe: Helsinki has problems with drug trafficking and use, although this seldom affects visitors. Violent crime targeting strangers seems to be on a rise, but severe incidents are few enough to often reach the headlines.

cities.d: a university town in Central Finland, beautifully set between lakes and ridges

x.around: Jyväskylä has invested in cycle and pedestrian routes. As the town centre is not big you might want to walk or cycle to see the sights. Almost 1/3 of the population of Jyväskylä are students who mainly use bicycles to get around in the central area. Roads are also in good condition. There are bicycle and car rentals in the city.

hidden.d: A nature preservation area just a few hundred meters off the city centre. The 700-m-long trail goes along river Tourujoki.
A small pond with usually relatively warm water. Swimming is possible also during the winter.
Toivola gives you a glimpse of what Jyväskylä used to look like in the early days. It is an old town dwelling consisting of the yard surrounded by traditional wooden craftsmen’s houses.
These are available and maintained in the winter once the ice is thick enough. The ice skating track is 2.5 km long, and the ski trail is 8 km long.

n.en: Ice skating and skiing on Lake Jyväsjärvi

hidden.d: A pine forest covered sand ridge in the center of the town is a nice place for a stroll or a picnic.

x.intro: Jyväskylä is a lively university city and the capital of Central Finland. About a third of the city's 148,000 inhabitants (2023) are students. Beautifully set between lakes and ridges, many motorsports fans are familiar with the city as the Neste Oil Rally of the World Rally Championships series takes place around the city each July. The works of the notable Finnish architect Alvar Aalto can be seen throughout the city.

must.d: Aircraft, engines and aircrew equipment which has been used by the Finnish Air Force. The Air Force Signals Museum. A large collection of scale models, photos etc..

n.fr: musée de l'aviation de Finlande centrale

must.d: A brand new permanent exhibition about the history and development of Central Finland. Changing historical and art exhibitions. The building has been designed by Alvar Aalto.
One of the station points on the world heritage listed Struve Geodetic Arc; a spectacular view over the Lake Päijänne from the observation tower on top of the Oravivuori hill.

next.d: a neighboring municipality with lots of lakes, nature reserves and activities.
in this town 40km to the west you can visit a UNESCO World Heritage Site: the magnificent example of rural building skills and peasant art in the old Petäjävesi church.

x.safe: The crime rate in Jyväskylä is generally low. However, it's best to avoid obviously drunk people during weekend nights after the bars close. Long queuing for taxis or late night snack sometimes frustrate some partygoers to seek fighting opponents. Sometimes this results to a temporary conversion from a pedestrian district to fighting arena, but the common sight of patrolling police makes the occurrences more rare.

cities.d: a technology city at the end of the Gulf of Bothnia

x.around: For 2024, the only e-scooter company in town is Ryde. Their operating area reaches from the southern region of Mäntylä all the way to Ideapark mall in Ritaharju. Be sure to follow the rules on riding and parking the vehicles.

hidden.d: Closed for renovation until 2026A great museum on the history of Northern Ostrobothnia, especially the history of Oulu. Exhibitions on four floors.

A car museum with 40 cars and 20 motorcycles and some traffic related paraphernalia on display. A couple of really interesting vehicles like the largest car ever built in the Nordic countries (a truck for a dam company), the…
Two-storey museum with a wide variety of modern artwork. Around 8 exhibits a year. Plenty of information in English, except for small, temporary exhibits.
In Sweden (to which Finland belonged from the 1300s to 1809), a "Kronomagasin" was a state-administered warehouse in which grain and other foodstuffs collected as tax were stored.
Built in 1908, the Oulujoki church is the only remaining wooden jugend church in Northern Finland. It is pretty, and a common wedding church. You can visit the church via Sunday masses at 10:00.
Plays in Finnish.
A museum of industrial history in Oulu. The museum is in an old drydock storage building.

The Sailor’s Home Museum is on the idyllic island of Pikisaari near downtown Oulu. The museum is in the oldest surviving wooden building in Oulu, also known as Matila House, and is the former home of sailor Isak Matilainen.

x.intro: Oulu (Swedish: Uleåborg) is the biggest city in Northern Finland, with about 210,000 inhabitants (in 2021). Once known for wood tar and salmon, Oulu has become a major high-tech centre, particularly in IT and wellness technology. Oulu has been selected as the European Capital of Culture for 2026.

must.d: Neoclassical Lutheran cathedral built in 1832 after its predecessor burned down. The architect Carl Ludvig Engel also designed the buildings of Senate Square in Helsinki.
Said to be the prettiest church in Oulu, and definitely stands out from its surroundings.

n.es: Iglesia de la Sagrada Familia de Nazaret
n.fr: église de la Sainte-Famille de Nazareth
n.it: chiesa della Santa Famiglia di Nazareth

must.d: The Finnish Co-educational Lycée of Oulu was established and opened in 1902 as a private Finnish-language lycée. It was the first co-educational upper secondary school in Oulu, a progressive learning institution at the time since…

next.d: is the largest island in the Gulf of Bothnia and a good destination for a day trip. A fixed road link from the mainland, composed of a causeway and two bridges, was opened in 2026 and replaced the…
by Finland's eastern border is a gateway to Lapland, with the ski resort Ruka, the legendary Karhunkierros hiking route (80 km) and Oulanka national park.
has a beautiful old town and is 35 km away.
municipality on the shores of Lake Oulujärvi about 90 km southeast of Oulu.
the capital of Finland

x.safe: Oulu is, on the whole, a very safe city, but avoid getting into arguments late in the night in fast food joints. Pickpocketing is remarkably rare, but it doesn't harm you to keep an eye on your belongings just like in any other place.

cities.d: largest wooden old town in the Nordics and a UNESCO World Heritage site

x.around: Since Rauma is a small town, walking around the city, and especially the old town, is easy. Bringing your own bicycle would be convenient.

hidden.d: This beautiful chapel was built by Kordelin's family and donated to the parish. It is in a very peaceful setting in the middle of the Old Cemetery.

n.en: Alfred Kordelin’s Burial Chapel and the Old Cemetery

hidden.d: A former Franciscan monastery, now a Lutheran church, built in the 15th century. Medieval wall and ceiling paintings.

Rauma's ice hockey team Lukko is in Finland's top league. Home games are played in winter at the Äijänsuo arena (Kivikylän tuhtitupa). Tickets from Lippupalvelu. The traditional arch-enemy is Ässät, a team from Pori.
A wooden tower overlooking the Syväraumanlahti bay with a tourist information centre offering info about island cruises.
Island groves can be seen here.

Also functioning as the city's water tower, has a beautiful manufactured waterfall on its grounds, and the view from the observation level café up on the water tower is likewise beautiful. Rauma souvenirs.
The workroom and home of a stove tile maker from the early 20th century.
Exhibitions about the history of seafaring.

x.intro: Rauma (Finnish) or Raumo (Swedish) is a town in Satakunta. The wooden houses in the centre of the old town are a UNESCO World Heritage site, as is the Bronze Age burial site Sammallahdenmäki about 20 km east of the centre. Rauma is the third oldest town in Finland, and has almost 40,000 inhabitants (2023). It is a historic seafaring town but in the 20th century paper milling became its main industry.

must.d: A Bronze Age burial site in the village of Kivikylä, well signposted off Highway 12 between Rauma and Tampere. While a of great archaeological significance ("The largest, most varied and complete burial site from the Scandinavian…

n.de: Grabstätten aus der Bronzezeit von Sammallahdenmäki
n.fr: site funéraire de l'âge du bronze de Sammallahdenmäki

must.d: Old Rauma is the largest uniform wooden town in the Nordic countries, and is a since the 550th anniversary of the city. The oldest inhabited buildings date back to the 17th century.

next.d: is in neighbouring Eurajoki. It has a visitor centre, open daily (but mind security procedures, you may need to register in advance). Occasionally there are bus tours from Rauma.

cities.d: gateway to Lapland and home of Santa Claus Village

x.around: Being not too big of a town, the best way to get around the city quickly is on foot. However, some of the main attractions are far away and buses are sparse; most households have a car.

hidden.d: Small-group tour operator offering Northern Lights excursions, snowmobile safaris, husky tours, reindeer experiences, hiking and national park tours.
Those attracted by northern forests will want to visit Pilke, where exhibitions describe sustainable use of northern forests and diverse yields, forest products and commodities.
The rebuilding of Rovaniemi after World War II was largely planned by the famous Finnish architect Alvar Aalto – particularly its reindeer antler layout.
This tiny (just 16 m long) arched bridge, completed in 1925, is the only bridge on the road to the Arctic Ocean that was not destroyed by German soldiers during the Lapland War 1944–1945.
In the village of Saarenkylä, on the top of Häkinvaara a stone-built kota, in front of which opens an amazing view over the rivers Ounasjoki and Kemijoki.
A small Orthodox church is on the other side of the Kemijoki river. Built 1957 and dedicated to Saint Apostle Andrew.
A fancy museum dedicated to forestry in Lapland from 1870 to the 1970s. The museum consist of old buildings brought here from all around the province, and the collections are inside the buildings.

x.intro: Rovaniemi, on the Arctic Circle, is the capital, transport hub and main commercial centre of Lapland, Finland's northernmost province. The city is 2,613 km (1,623 mi) south of the North Pole. It is a highly popular tourist destination and is considered to be the official home town of Santa Claus.

must.d: Located right on the old computed place of the Arctic Circle (now computed to be 2 km north), this is a tourist trap if there ever was one – but few tourists can miss the chance to meet Santa Claus.
Underground amusement park within walking distance from Santa Claus Village. Open only during the winter season.
One of the best museums and science centres in Finland, focusing on life in the Arctic regions through the ages as well as the Sami culture, history of Finnish Lapland and Rovaniemi city.

Accomplished in 1989, the bridge has become one of the most important symbols of Rovaniemi. It runs over the Kemijoki close the northern end of the city centre. The bridge has a high pylon with bright yellow light on top.
Built 1950, near the administrative centre. Famous for its considerable large fresco "Spring of the Life" by professor Lennart Segerstråle.
Art, music and other culture events. The art museum collection consists mostly of modern Finnish art. Home of the Chamber Orchestra of Lapland.

A 16-m-high waterfall and old-growth forest. Bus stop at the road, parking area 1 km farther. A 50-m steep trail for wheelchairs (assistance needed) to a hut with view to the rapids, a 3.5-km nature trail through varying terrain,…

This is the final resting place for 2,683 German soldiers who died during the World War II in Lapland. Constructed of large stone blocks and located virtually in the middle of nowhere, it seems to be of interest to some, as there…

next.d: (near Kittilä), Luosto (near Sodankylä) and Pyhä (near Pelkosenniemi).
with an Arctic wildlife park
the Finnish capital for the Sámi, 315 km farther north

x.safe: Rovaniemi is a safe city. You're unlikely to face any major dangers. For hiking or off-the-beaten-path destinations, follow common advice: tell somebody about your plans and a hard deadline, and know what you are doing.

cities.d: a small lakeside town with a big castle and a popular opera festival.

x.around: Savonlinna is stretched out on a series of islands in the middle of Lake Saimaa. While you can cover the central parts on foot, you'll need to resort to buses (or rent a car) to access the suburbs. If you want to rent a car, there is a Hertz rental office at the waterfront, near Hotel Tott. Savonlinna is surrounded by lakes and you can also rent a canoe to paddle around town centre.

hidden.d: Built as an Orthodox church in 1846, transformed into a Lutheran church in 1938. The church was returned to the orthodox parish in 2022.

A nice way to see the city and its surroundings is from a small cruise ship. There are cruises of an hour or an hour and a half around the city or the surrounding archipelago, leaving every half an hour or so all day, some with…
On Riihisaari island you can learn more about the cultural history and the nature of the region around Lake Saimaa and also visit the natural exhibition of the governmental forest service.
Islands close to the city centre, a popular place among the locals for getting out in the nature. Hiking paths and places for swimming and barbecuing.

x.intro: Savonlinna (Swedish: Nyslott) is a small city in South Savonia province, Eastern Finland, close to the Russian border. Savonlinna is one of the iconic tourism destinations of Finland with traditions of hospitality going back to the 19th century. The town has been attracting visitors with its spa, lake nature including two national parks. In summertime the town offers rich variety of lake cruises, many still operated with old lake steamers.

must.d: Medieval Olavinlinna is the city's symbol and main attraction. Built in 1475 by Danish knight Erik Axelsson to protect the eastern border of the Swedish-Danish Kalmar Union, it was named after the patron saint of knights, St.
The cathedral is Savonlinna's main church, opened in 1879. The church had a bishop in the years 1896–1924 and hence gained the right to bear the name cathedral.

next.d: see the iconic Finnish national landscape
see world's largest wooden church
idyllic village between Savonia and Karelia along Saimaa waterways
a small municipality about 30 km north of Savonlinna
relax in the spa resort Järvisydän and enjoy the natural wonders of Linnansaari national park.
venue of an annual big rowing competition with traditional boats

intro: Finland (Finnish: Suomi, Swedish: Finland) is a country with vast areas of unspoiled nature speckled with comfortable small towns and cities. Scraped flat by sheets of ice during several ice ages, Finland lacks the dramatic mountains and fjords of its Nordic neighbours but makes up for it with 188,000 lakes and a similar number of islands. Finland extends into the Arctic, where the Northern Lights and the Midnight Sun can be seen.

other.d: scenic national park in Eastern Finland, symbol for the nature of the country

x.around: There is an extensive trail network, including a few nature trails (i.e. with information boards). There are also some roads in the park, but parking is allowed only in designated areas. Cycling is allowed on some routes.
x.intro: Koli National Park (Kolin kansallispuisto) lies in the municipalities of Joensuu, Lieksa and Kontiolahti in North Karelia, Eastern Finland, on the western shore of Lake Pielinen, and covers 3,000 hectares.
x.safe: The cliffs may be slippery, especially when wet, and the slopes steep. Take care.

other.d: pint-sized but pretty national park a stone's throw from Helsinki

x.around: Although deviating from trails is allowed, the park is small enough that the trails suffice for most of it – end visited enough that you should avoid tear of the ground off trails.
x.intro: Nuuksio National Park (Finnish: Nuuksion kansallispuisto, Swedish: Noux nationalpark) is in Southern Finland on the outskirts of Espoo and the neighbouring municipalities of Kirkkonummi and Vihti, 35 km from Helsinki. It is one of two national parks reaching into the capital region (the other is Sipoonkorpi National Park).
x.safe: Apart from vipers and the very remote chance of meeting a bear, there is little dangerous fauna in the park. Thanks to the swampy terrain, mosquitoes can be a nuisance, so stock up on the bug spray. Stay on the main trails if you don't have a compass and orienteering experience.

other.d: "the Arm of Finland" offers scenic views and the highest hills in Finland

x.around: The village is built along E8 (here called Käsivarrentie) over a distance of several kilometres, with a significant gap between the north-west and south-east concentrations. Check that your accommodation is reasonably close to the services you need. There are no other significant roads.

hidden.d: The highest point of the Finnish national road network, 565.8 m above sea level. A Lapland War memorial by the nearby rest spot.

Return trip by boat from Kilpisjärvi to Koltalahti and 3 km hike to the tripoint: the boat trip over Kilpisjärvi takes half an hour (with nice views) and the boat waits two hours while the passengers visit the tripoint.
1.1 km (to one direction) trail leading from the village to the top of Salmivaara hill. The trail starts along a sports trail and forks off into the birch "forest" after a few hundred meters.
Research station of the University of Helsinki, founded 1964.

Information on the wilderness area, the Saana fell and the Malla nature reserve by the tripoint. Maps (also for nearby areas in Norway and Sweden), fishing permits, snowmobile track permits, reservation and key of reservation…
Perhaps the world's easiest palsa bog to visit. Right next to the highway with parking lot and an easy-to-access 500-m nature trail. Palsa bogs contain permanently frozen ice lenses under the soil.

x.intro: Kilpisjärvi (Northern Sámi: Gilbbesjávri) is a small village in Enontekiö, Finland's "arm", the only real alpine village in Finland. Several sights are located in Kilpisjärvi or nearby. The village has about one hundred year-round inhabitants but many more summer residents. Kilpisjärvi is clearly a summer destination, although in winter used as base for tour skiing in the adjacent wilderness area.

must.d: Probably the most well-known mountain in Finland. A 4-km trail and the longest stairs in Finland take you to the very top of the 1000-metre Arctic hill with a weird shape.

next.d: long distance hiking route, via Halti to Kautokeino in Norway or via the tripoint to Abisko and further on over the Narvik fells and through Laponia.

other.d: Saariselkä and Ylläs — popular winter sports resorts in Lapland

x.around: Levi has a bus system called Ski Bus with two routes marked R1 and R2. Ski Bus runs from November to May. A Ski Bus ticket is included to the ski lift pass for €3/day. Otherwise, a day ticket for bus bought from ZeroPoint costs €4. From the bus you can only buy single ride tickets for €4 (2021). In the Levi centre you can easily walk or ski around.
x.intro: Levi is one of the biggest winter sport resorts in Finland. It is in the Kittilä municipality in Lapland, by the village Sirkka. Levi is a very popular place among young people, and in addition to being a ski resort it is a significant nightlife centre for people from rural Lapland.

next.d: some 20 km away by ski. The park is the third largest and the most visited one in the country, with many more services than in most national parks in Finland.
